answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network elects a beacon committee via game-theoretic multi-agent auditing to conduct topological cut verifications. Auditing agents analyze graph connectivity to identify clustered partitions where attackers mirror identities. Suspicious clusters undergo stake slashing, driving the adversary's capital efficiency to a nadir. Because isolating verified cuts requires superlinear attacker cost scaling with $O(N^2)$ stake commitments, fabricated nodes become economically unviable.
